defects.title: AC-C1 uses escaped pipes, so raw command matches nothing and cannot fail
defects.what_goes_wrong: Copied as written, the ERE treats \| as a literal bar so no real `orca orchestration ...` line matches (verified: exit 1, no output on `orca-ide worktree list`), and the `\| grep -v` stage is not a shell pipe, so the SA-2/WC-8 gate passes vacuously; the same \| shell-pipe form recurs in AC-C4, AC-C5 and AC-0.3. Some covered gids also raise the core-scope conflict (see c14-d3).
defects.is_fixed_when: AC-C1 (and the other checks using shell pipes) is given in a form that, copied from the raw file text, uses real `|` alternation and real pipes (for example in a fenced block) and is shown to match a planted `orca orchestration ...` line.
defects.deletion_note: No: deleting AC-C1 would leave SA-2 and WC-8 without any mechanical gate.
defects.present_in_others_hint: AC-C4 (line 175), AC-C5 (176) and AC-0.3 (193) use the same \| shell-pipe form; SA-2 and WC-8 cite AC-C1 as their check.

defects.title: Additive-edit check '^-[^-]' misses deleted bullet and --- lines
defects.what_goes_wrong: A deleted markdown bullet `- x` or frontmatter `---` appears in a diff as `-- x` / `----`, whose second character is `-`, so the filter prints nothing and AC-C5/AC-0.3 report 'additive' after existing lines were removed or rewritten (verified in a scratch dir).
defects.is_fixed_when: The additive-edit check flags any deleted line except the `--- a/<file>` diff header (for example by excluding only that header or using git diff --numstat deletions), so a removed bullet or `---` line makes it print output.
defects.deletion_note: No: removing the check would leave SA-1/SA-4/SA-5 unenforced.
defects.present_in_others_hint: Both AC-C5 (line 176) and AC-0.3 (line 193) use the filter; SA-4 and SA-5 are the requirements it guards.

defects.title: AC-C1 scans core/, where SA-2 allows and P0 requires Orca text
defects.quote: The only allowed mention of Orca in a changed command is as an example of a caller's question channel inside the contract file.
defects.what_goes_wrong: AC-C1 greps src/superclaude/core (exempting only ccsession-tag) with pass condition 'prints nothing', yet SA-2 permits an Orca question-channel example in core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md (the spec's own example is `orca orchestration ask`, line 29) and P0 adds an Orca section to core/HOW-WE-WORK.md, so the common check fails on permitted content in every phase; SA-2 also says 'changed command' for a file that is not a command.
defects.is_fixed_when: AC-C1's scope matches SA-2 (commands, skills, agents only) or it names WORKER-CONTRACT.md and the HOW-WE-WORK Orca section as exempt, and SA-2 states whether core files are covered by the no-Orca-command rule.
defects.deletion_note: No: dropping core from the scan without saying so, or deleting the SA-2 allowance, only moves the conflict; the scope and the allowance must be stated consistently.
defects.present_in_others_hint: SA-2 (147), SA-5 (150), P0 row (158), contract file location (52), AC-C1 (172).

defects.title: AC-C1 checks only four orca subcommands while SA-2 bans any orca command
defects.quote: No command, skill or agent file runs an `orca` or `orca-ide` command
defects.what_goes_wrong: The AC-C1 pattern covers only orchestration, worktree, terminal and agent, so a file running `orca status`, `orca open` or `orca-ide skills get ...` (real commands per orca-capabilities.md) violates SA-2 yet passes the gate.
defects.is_fixed_when: AC-C1's pattern matches any `orca`/`orca-ide` invocation (or the spec states that only these four verbs are banned and SA-2 is narrowed to match).
defects.deletion_note: No: deleting SA-2 or the check removes the standalone-use guarantee rather than aligning them.
